what: Viper Energy owns mineral and royalty interests under oil and gas wells in the Permian basin. It does not drill: it owns the land rights and receives a share of what producers extract, with no drilling costs.
customers: Its income comes from oil and gas producers operating on acreage it owns the minerals under, largely Diamondback Energy.
money: a share of oil and gas production from wells on its acreage
moat: Mineral interests under the best Permian acreage, which produce income for the life of each well without any capital or operating cost.
risks: Oil and gas prices set earnings
Debt of about $2.4 billion after large acquisitions of minerals
Diamondback controls it, so minority holders have limited influence
Production depends on operators choosing to drill its acreage
opportunities: Revenue grew about 62% last year as acquired minerals were added
A distribution yield around 5% with no drilling costs to fund
Analysts see about 39% upside from current levels
watch: Royalty production volumes and the number of wells being drilled on its acreage.
